body:
I compared  
Airflow 3.2.x python 3.12 constraints (https://github.com/apache/airflow/blob/constraints-3-2/constraints-3.12.txt) with  
Airflow 3.3.x python 3.12 constraints (https://github.com/apache/airflow/blob/constraints-3-3/constraints-3.12.txt)

Downgrades I found (left is `constraints-3-2`, right is `constraints-3-3`):

- `apache-airflow-providers-databricks==7.15.0` -> `apache-airflow-providers-databricks==6.13.0`
- `databricks-sql-connector==4.2.5` -> `databricks-sql-connector==2.0.2`
  - `databricks-sql-connector` is a dependency of `apache-airflow-providers-databricks`
- `numpy==2.4.6` -> `numpy==1.26.4`
- `pandas==2.3.3` -> `pandas==2.1.4`

Apart from that, the diffs for python 3.11 and 3.12 look more weird in general: https://github.com/apache/airflow/compare/constraints-3-2..constraints-3-3

> I think there should be something near the latest version 7.16.1. I don't know if this intended or if there might be a deeper issue because with Airflow 3.2.x, a proper version is included.

There is no way to do that. The versions are decided by PIP resolution algorithm. As long as versions are compatible that is acceptable.

You can always generate your own constraints file. You don't have to use the one provided by Airflow.

issue.title: Relax the <= 0.23.0 limit of thrift
issue.body:
The reason for keeping thrift to <= 0.23.0 is solved - see https://github.com/apache/thrift/pull/3584 and thrift 0.24.0 has been released with wheels published (so this double-solves the problem as in most cases no setup.py is even called).

It caused some unwanted downgrades in Airflow - to the version of databricks-sql-connector that did not have this limitation: 

See  https://github.com/apache/airflow/issues/69603

We are workarounding it in Airflow, but it would be great to get newer versions of databricks-sql-connector to support thrift >= 0.24.0

issue.title: Pin databricks-sql-connector>=4.0.0 in generated constraints

repository.name: airflow
repository.description: Apache Airflow - A platform to programmatically author, schedule, and monitor workflows

issue.body:
During highest-resolution constraint generation, the resolver preferred the newest `thrift` (0.24.0, from apache/thrift#3584) over the newest `databricks-sql-connector`. Because current `databricks-sql-connector` requires `thrift<=0.23.0`, the resolver downgraded the connector — which in turn dragged the `databricks` provider back to an old version in the PyPI constraints.

Pinning `databricks-sql-connector>=4.0.0` in `additional_constraints_for_highest_resolution` keeps the constraints installable with a current connector and provider.

Tracked upstream at databricks/databricks-sql-python#859.

closes: #69603

body:
> I stand by my comment that users can just create thier own constraints file.

@eladkal Yes, I you are right, it is easy to create own constraints. 

But releasing an official version with a _**broken**_ constraint is something that is against the idea of constraints by itself.

What are constraints for?  
To write down a specific configuration of environment that is tested and known working together correctly (as far as bugs are known yet).

>  But releasing an official version with a broken constraint is something that is against the idea of constraints by itself.

I think we defer on the interpretation of broken :)
If @potiuk think it's needed and it's risk free then I am fine with it.
I will keep the issue open till we decide one way or the other
Since it's more than 2 weeks for 3.3.1 - I think it's worth fixing it in relased image and announcement in users@ list

The databricks provider downgrade on the Airflow 3.3.0 constraints for Python 3.11 and 3.12 has been fixed.

**Root cause:** the constraints pinned `thrift==0.23.0`, which conflicts with `databricks-sql-connector` 4.x (`thrift<0.21.0`). During resolution the newer thrift was kept and the connector was downgraded to `2.0.2`, which in turn dragged `apache-airflow-providers-databricks` back to `6.13.0` (Oct 2024). Python 3.10/3.13/3.14 were unaffected.

**Fix** — the Python 3.11 and 3.12 pins were brought in line with the other interpreters:
- `apache-airflow-providers-databricks` 6.13.0 → 7.16.1
- `databricks-sql-connector` 2.0.2 → 4.2.5
- `thrift` 0.23.0 → 0.16.0

This was applied to both the `constraints-3.3.0` tag and the rolling `constraints-3-3` branch. The generator-side fix that prevents recurrence (pinning `databricks-sql-connector>=4.0.0` during constraint generation) is already on `v3-3-test` (#69871). The published 3.3.0 images are being refreshed with the corrected constraints.
